findings.message: Other modules call `weekTotals` and `projectHours`, but these functions take only a `tx` and return every person's hours, status and name in the tenant. No caller viewer is passed and no data scope is applied. architecture.md says that 'Cross-module reads go through contract functions, which apply the caller's data scope'. Fix: take the caller's Viewer or ServiceContext, then filter rows the same way `seesWeek`/`time:team` does. Alternatively, publish only aggregates with no per-person data.
findings.scenario: An Employee-scoped module (or finance code acting for a user without time:team) calls weekTotals(tx, 2026-W42). It gets back Nimal, Kasun, Ayesha, Tharushi and Dinesh with their hours and statuses, although teamWeek would show that user nothing.

findings.message: Week totals are worked out two ways that can disagree. TeamRow.total (and so the lede, the This week card and the 'Approve N submitted (X h)' button) adds up only the five Mon–Fri `perDay` cells. myWeek.total, weekHours (the submit payload) and the weekTotals contract add up every entry in the week. logTime takes any YYYY-MM-DD, including Saturday and Sunday, and its default 'today' can be a weekend. Fix: either reject weekend days in logTime, or show 7 days and compute every total from all the entries.
findings.scenario: On Saturday 2026-10-17, chat 'log 4 h on FLT' (no day) creates a 4 h entry in W42. My timesheet shows a total of 4.0 h with no visible cell for it. The Team row for the same week shows 0 more hours, and the approver approves a week whose shown total is 4 h short.

findings.message: When no day is given, the default is `isoDate(new Date())`, which is the UTC date and not the person's local date. For tenants east or west of UTC, time logged near midnight lands on the wrong day, and on a Monday or Sunday it can land in a different ISO week. `today()` in ui/parts.tsx has the same UTC assumption. Fix: resolve 'today' in the tenant's or user's time zone, or require the caller to give a day.
findings.scenario: A Colombo user (+05:30) logs 2 h through chat at 03:00 on Monday 2026-10-19. The entry is dated 2026-10-18 (Sunday) and goes into 2026-W42, an already-submitted or approved week, instead of W43.

findings.message: guardLock blocks writes only when the week is 'approved'. Entries can still be added to a 'submitted' week. The approver then approves hours the person never submitted, and the WeekSubmitted.hours payload no longer matches. Fix: refuse logTime on submitted weeks, or move the week back to draft and require it to be submitted again.
findings.scenario: Nimal submits W42 with 31.5 h (event hours = 31.5). Nimal then logs 8 h more on CON for 2026-10-16. Maya approves, and the locked week now holds 39.5 h, while the submitted record says 31.5 h.

findings.message: The README rule 'you never approve your own week' is applied in chainFor, but the locked-change path lets any time:admin holder add hours to their own approved week. Those hours then sit in an approved, locked week that nobody else approved. Fix: in guardLock, reject a locked change when week.user_id is the actor's own user.
findings.scenario: Sahan (Admin) has W42 approved by a manager at 30 h. Sahan logs 10 h more for themselves on 2026-10-16. The call succeeds and W42 stays 'approved' at 40 h.

findings.message: findWeek matches `person` by email OR by a case-insensitive person_name, then takes the first row. When two people share a name, approve_week, reject_week, remind_week and reopen_week act on whichever row comes first. Fix: fetch all matches and throw when there is more than one ('which Nimal Silva? use their email').
findings.scenario: The tenant has two people named 'Nimal Silva', and both have a W42 week. approve_week {person:'Nimal Silva', week:'2026-W42'} approves an arbitrary one of them, possibly not the week the approver meant.

findings.message: `wk()` turns a well-formed but non-existent ISO week into `undefined`, so get_team_week and get_my_week quietly fall back to the latest week. TeamPage and MyPage do the same with `parseWeekKey(params.week) ?? undefined`. Malformed input should produce an error (weekOrNow in server/weeks.ts already throws for this), not a different week's data.
findings.scenario: get_my_week {week:'2025-W53'} (2025 has no week 53) returns W42's data instead of an error, and the agent reports it as week 53. Likewise, /time/w/2026-W60 renders W42.

findings.message: The retention entries use class 'personal'. That is not one of the 002 sensitivity classes the module standard lists (pay, health, bank, performance, candidate). Reject comments and approval decisions are arguably 'performance'. Use a real 002 class so masking and retention apply.

The CSV export wraps personName in quotes without escaping any embedded `"`, and it does not neutralise a leading `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`. A name containing a quote breaks the row, and one starting with '=' becomes a spreadsheet formula. Double embedded quotes and prefix formula characters with an apostrophe.
findings.scenario: A personName of '=HYPERLINK("http://x","a")' runs as a formula when the export is opened in Excel.

findings.message: A bulk approve or remind runs each week in its own transaction. If one week fails (for example, another approver handled it first), the weeks before it stay committed, the rest are skipped and the action throws, so the result is partial with only one generic error shown. Fix: run them in one transaction, or report each week's outcome.
findings.scenario: For 'Approve 3 submitted', Nimal is already approved by someone else. Kasun gets approved, Nimal throws 'is approved, not submitted', and Ayesha is never attempted.

findings.message: logTime only checks whether the week is 'approved'. Anyone can still add entries to a week that is 'submitted', and the week stays submitted. The approver then approves and locks hours that were not there when the week was submitted. The WeekSubmitted payload also keeps the old total. Fix: when someone logs into a submitted week, either reject the write or move the week back to draft (with audit and an event). Add a test that logs into a submitted week.
findings.scenario: Nimal submits W42 with 31.5 h, so time.week.submitted says hours=31.5. Over MCP, Nimal then calls log_time FLT 2026-10-16 8 h, and the week is still 'submitted'. Maya approves from the Team page, which locks 39.5 h, but only 31.5 h were ever submitted.

findings.message: The README says reminders reach people through notification rules. The manifest declares no notification rule for time.week.reminded, so 'Remind N people' only writes an event that nothing consumes. Fix: add the rule (plain manifest data), or say in the README that reminders are not delivered yet.
findings.scenario: Maya clicks 'Remind 2 people', and no one receives anything.
